Neurodegenerative parkinsonian syndrome; gaze palsy reflects central motor dysfunction rather than damage to the eye.
Inherited metabolic disorder defined by hyperammonemic encephalopathy; biochemical liver localization does not establish hepatic damage.
Vertebral skeletal dysplasia with platyspondyly and scoliosis; corneal opacities and endocrine manifestations are rare across this umbrella.
Degenerative disease of articular cartilage, adjacent bone and synovium; not an autoimmune disorder.
Motor neuron disease with denervation-associated skeletal muscle atrophy in 5/10. Dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction; respiratory failure occurs in 1/10.
Primary progressive skeletal muscular dystrophy with finger/toe movement limitation; cataracts are reported but their frequency is not established in the supplied evidence.
Intellectual disability and characteristic ptosis define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 80-99%. Additional ocular damage includes cataracts in 3/8.
Primary bronchopulmonary adenocarcinoma; no evidence establishes common direct damage to another organ.
Architecture-defined carcinoma umbrella without a fixed organ; representative breast carcinomas have no axis, while salivary origin is subtype-specific.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; retinal dysplasia in 2/4. Renal dysplasia occurs in 1/4, below threshold.
Chronic middle-ear disease; the umbrella includes non-suppurative forms and does not uniformly establish infection or an immune-mediated mechanism.
Pontocerebellar maldevelopment and neurodegeneration with seizures, developmental disability and spasticity; contracture frequency is unspecified.
Benign neoplasm originating in ocular structures, including eyelids and lacrimal glands.
Inherited peripheral nerve degeneration; chronic denervation produces defining distal skeletal muscle atrophy in most patients.
ADHD is a neurodevelopmental disorder within the neurologic axis; developmental delay is also reported in 1/3.
Qualitative or quantitative von Willebrand factor deficiency causes a coagulation disorder; bleeding sites do not establish intrinsic organ disease.
Muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; cleft palate directly affects oral structure in 1/3 reported patients, near the threshold.
Testicular germ-cell malignancy arises in a reproductive organ, without defining endocrine dysfunction; most presentations are localized.
Immune-mediated photodermatosis involving a delayed cutaneous hypersensitivity response to sunlight.
Defining CNS, renal and skeletal triad; hepatic fibrosis occurs in 80-99%. Ocular malformations and cleft palate occur in 30-79% but are omitted by the four-axis cap.
Malignant neuroendocrine paraganglionic tumor of the jugular/tympanic region; vascular proximity and variable metastatic sites do not establish additional organ axes.
B-cell developmental defect with reduced B-cell counts in 2/2 and absent immunoglobulins; recurrent respiratory and ear infections are separately diagnosed diseases.
Umbrella of adult interstitial lung diseases; extrapulmonary involvement and immune or hematologic mechanisms depend on the subtype.
Fungal infection directly inflames the esophageal mucosa; associated immunodeficiency or diabetes is a separate disease.
